views.reconstructed_statement: For every function a:R->R, suppose that for every t in R, -1<=t implies that t<=1 implies cos(a(t))=t. Then, for every x in R, let U_x=[[cos(a(x)),-sin(a(x))],[sin(a(x)),cos(a(x))]], regarded as a complex matrix with row and column indices Fin 2. The following three statements hold together: (1) U_x is unitary, meaning U_x^dagger U_x=I_2; (2) U_x(0,0) equals the complex embedding of x if and only if -1<=x and x<=1; (3) if 1<|x|, U_x(0,0) does not equal the complex embedding of x. The conclusion quantifies over every real x, including x outside [-1,1].

Use the ordered composite index J=C x (S x X), and define T(B)=I_C tensor (B tensor I_X); let A apply V(s,x) to C while keeping s and x fixed; let Q send the column basis vector (c,(s,x)) to (c,(s,pi_s(x))). Then all three conclusions hold: (1) T(P)^dagger*(Q*(A*T(P))) is unitary on J; (2) for every complex S-by-S matrix B, if B is unitary, T(B)*(Q*(A*T(P))) is unitary on J; (3) for every complex S-by-S matrix D, if D*P=I_S, then D=P^dagger. B in the second conclusion has no required relation to P. D in the third conclusion has no separate unitarity hypothesis. These two universal quantifiers are distinct bindings of the formal name other, and all three conclusions share both initial hypotheses.
